pr_title: Automated cherry pick of #93044: Initialize scheduler's podInformer in sharedInformerFactory
pr_body:
Cherry pick of #93044 and #93566 on release-1.19.

#93044: Initialize scheduler's podInformer in sharedInformerFactory

#93566: Optimize the use of informer for scheduler

/sig scheduling
/kind bug

Because of the use of 2 separate informers, the scheduler might try to schedule a Pod, fail and never retry, because it thinks that the Pod doesn't exist. Reality was that the Pod was not yet added to the 2nd informer.

This is solved by using a single informer. This fix was originally introduced in 1.20 as a memory optimization, but it turns out to guarantee correct behavior.

#93566 is supposed to just be a refactoring. However, since we don't this would be the last 1.19 release, it's better to include it, as we have signal that both changes work well in production.

Fixes #104521

```release-note
Fix a regression in 1.19 where a race condition in scheduler could make a new unschedulable Pod never be retried.
```

issue_context.title: Pods stuck in Pending status - kube-scheduler 1.19.13
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:
After upgrading core k8s components from 1.18 to 1.19.13 we faced a problem with Pending pods. From time to time PODs(different deployments) are stuck in Pending status. From kube-scheduler logs, we see a new event that starts appearing after the upgrade. For example `Pod kube-system/prometheus-thanos-frontend-86f4f8df77-h52tl **doesn't exist in informer cache**: pod "prometheus-thanos-frontend-86f4f8df77-h52tl" not found`.
However, ClusterAutoscaler still tries checking if there's an appropriate node `Pod kube-system.prometheus-thanos-frontend-86f4f8df77-h52tl marked as unschedulable can be scheduled on node ***.eu-west-1.compute.internal (based on hinting). Ignoring in scale up.`

It looks like kube-scheduler just forgot about the pod, because after a couple of attempts it stop trying to schedule the pod and we see no logs/events for hours. On the other hand, CA still tries to schedule it even spin up a new nodes.

#### What you expected to happen:

Pending pods are assigned to nodes.

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

We don't see any pattern. It happens time to time for a completely different deployments.

#### Anything else we need to know?:

If we restart kube-scheduler so the leader is changed the Pending Pods are being successfully scheduled.

#### Environment:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):
```
Client Version: version.Info{Major:"1", Minor:"20", GitVersion:"v1.20.0", GitCommit:"af46c47ce925f4c4ad5cc8d1fca46c7b77d13b38", GitTreeState:"clean", BuildDate:"2020-12-08T17:59:43Z", GoVersion:"go1.15.5", Compiler:"gc", Platform:"darwin/amd64"}

```
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: AWS
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS Linux 7 (Core)
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`): Linux ***.eu-west-1.compute.internal 3.10.0-1160.25.1.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Wed Apr 28 21:49:45 UTC 2021 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug): 
- Others: ClusterAutoscaler 1.19.1, kube-scheduler 1.19.13
comments: /sig scheduling
Are you sure the pods in question still exist? The error "doesn't exist in informer cache" indicates that the pod doesn't exist anymore.
it would be great if you have a concrete repro steps

@ahg-g, I work on the same team as @YuraHrunyk. I just wanted to clarify a bit the work-around we use to recover from this situation. All we do is kill the kube-scheduler process which is currently the leader. Then, one of the other redundant schedulers acquires the leader  lease and the pod gets scheduled right away.

We have thousands of pods getting scheduled across hundreds of nodes and this happens only very occasionally. We aren't quite sure how we could reproduce this because there isn't a clear pattern. Any guidance you have there would be appreciated.

This is interesting, the issue is that the scheduler thinks that the pod doesn't exist anymore because it can't find it in the informer cache, and so it is ignoring it completely. 

In https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/90660, we removed some retry logic that perhaps masked the issue you are facing. 

@liggitt I have a couple of questions:
1) If a pod used to exist in the informer cache, is there any reason that it would *temporarily* cease to exist?
2) Is it possible to have a race where we receive a pod add event, but the pod may not be readily be accessible via the pod lister (the event handler and lister are both setup from the same pod informer)?

@matthias50 can you tell us a bit more about your setup? are deploying k8s manually? do you have the scheduler running on the same VM as the api-server?

/cc @Huang-Wei @alculquicondor

> If a pod used to exist in the informer cache, is there any reason that it would temporarily cease to exist?

Not that I know of. The client state (the store used by the pod lister) handles updates and relists by replacing existing content, it doesn't remove and re-add objects (_and_ it does so under lock)

> Is it possible to have a race where we receive a pod add event, but the pod may not be readily be accessible via the pod lister (the event handler and lister are both setup from the same pod informer)?

Not that I know of... the store is updated before the event handler is called

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34fb61beba52d9e1ab3f044a7be8b9f49d99534e/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L399-L402

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34fb61beba52d9e1ab3f044a7be8b9f49d99534e/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L404-L407

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34fb61beba52d9e1ab3f044a7be8b9f49d99534e/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/controller.go#L410-L413

It is possible for the event handler to encounter a store that has already processed the *next* event received from the API server, so the following is possible:
1. pod is updated
2. pod is deleted
3. scheduler observes update event
4. scheduler updates pod in store
5. scheduler enqueues call to OnUpdate
6. scheduler observes delete event
7. scheduler removes pod from store
8. scheduler enqueues call to OnDelete
9. OnUpdate is called, looks in store, cannot find pod
10. OnDelete is called, looks in store, cannot find pod

The error message was logged here:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34fb61beba52d9e1ab3f044a7be8b9f49d99534e/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L400-L405

and it was introduced in 1.19.

Regarding the root cause, one thing to note is: the podLister used here is "filtered" (`status.phase!=Succeeded,status.phase!=Failed`) - all the way from scheduler's instantiation:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/34fb61beba52d9e1ab3f044a7be8b9f49d99534e/pkg/scheduler/scheduler.go#L756-L763

So is it possible that the pod somehow falls outside the indexer (i.e., treated as `status.phase==Succeeded` or `status.phase==Failed`), so scheduler cannot get the desired pod?

@YuraHrunyk could you verify what's the eventual `status.phase` of the pending pods, and if by any chance, the _interim_ `status.phase` when the "xxx doesn't exist in informer cache" log was firstly spotted?

BTW: in 1.18, the pod was obtained from [a live API query](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f3e19b7beb1cc0110255668c4238ed63dadb7ad/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L498) instead of "filtered" podLister.
/triage accepted

@Huang-Wei notice they mentioned that the pod did get eventually scheduled when switching the leader.

@YuraHrunyk  can you also please verify that the same pod, not a replacement one, was eventually scheduled?

is it the informer cache / lister the pods are missing from, or the caches maintained by these:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ebb9fafac620dac6e632b7b2607d575cc1df926f/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L280-L329

if so, is it possible the filtering is dropping events needed to maintain those caches accurately, or could something like  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/ebb9fafac620dac6e632b7b2607d575cc1df926f/pkg/scheduler/eventhandlers.go#L216-L217 explain why the pod is seen as missing elsewhere?

It is not missing from the scheduler's maintained cache, it is missing from the pod informer cache, here is the failed lookup: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/44a3aa90a777aa05e997cb827744597c06b70803/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L469) 

this pod informer is configured to exclude pods that ran to completion: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/44a3aa90a777aa05e997cb827744597c06b70803/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L432

@YuraHrunyk can you provide all the logs referring to the pod that "disappears"? I would like to know if we tried to schedule it at other points. That might help us narrow down the possible race conditions.
Logs from the apiserver would help too.

>  can you also please verify that the same pod, not a replacement one, was eventually scheduled?

@ahg-g @YuraHrunyk I can verify that it is the same pod, not a replacement one.

> can you tell us a bit more about your setup? are deploying k8s manually? do you have the scheduler running on the same VM as the api-server?

@ahg-g, we are deploying k8s using home grown automation on AWS. All our clusters have three master nodes (AWS instances), each with static pods for the k8s control plane components (kube-scheduler, kube-apiserver, kube-controller-manager).

Here is a summary on the underlying problem across releases:

- in k8s versions <= 1.19, scheduler maintains two podInformers - one is from the sharedInformerFactory the other is created independently (code of v1.19.14 below). This is problematic.
    https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0fd2b5afdfe3134d6e1531365fdb37dd11f54d1c/cmd/kube-scheduler/app/options/options.go#L288-L289
- in theory, the problem (described in this issue) should surface in all versions, but why it's only reported until 1.19? It's because in the versions <= 1.18, we call API server directly in the error handling logic (instead of podLister). And API server always has the source of truth (code of v1.18.20 below)
    https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1f3e19b7beb1cc0110255668c4238ed63dadb7ad/pkg/scheduler/factory.go#L498
- what happened in 1.19? You may have noticed that we removed the direct API call (as unneeded API server queries is an anti-pattern), and use the podLister instead. It's supposed to work properly, but without querying API server, the 2 podInformer must be unified; otherwise, the 2 independent informers may have racing issues, as what this issue reported.
- what happened in 1.20? We unified the 2 podInformers and thought that was a _good-to-have_ fix, but it turns out to be a must. So Aldo raised #105015 to back port the fix to 1.19.
